newsitem.title: USA: Senate adopts bill to shield volunteers.
newsitem.headline: Senate adopts bill to shield volunteers.

text.p: The Senate, emerging from several days of gridlock on Thursday, approved a bill shielding volunteers from negligence lawsuits.

The legislation had been before the Senate since last Friday, but was stalled by a filibuster by Democrats angry that Republicans were holding up the nomination of Alexis Herman as President Clinton's labour secretary. Herman was confirmed on Wednesday.
Passage of the so-called Volunteer Protection Act on a 99-1 vote followed a Philadelphia conference on volunteerism opened by President Clinton on Monday.
Proponents of the bill said that potential volunteers were disouraged from giving their services because of the fear that they might be sued for negligence if an accident occurred.

The bill provides that a volunteer of a nonprofit organisation or government would be relieved of liability for harm in simple negligence cases. Cases involving such actions as hate crimes or wilful misconduct would not be protected.
Before voting on the bill, the Senate adopted an amendment clarifying its provisions to meet the concerns of some senators that it was too broad.
